subsystems.name: Analyte sensing layer
subsystems.role: detects glucose, cortisol and other markers without drawing blood.
parts: optical emitters and photodetectors (near-infrared, Raman) for glucose
electrochemical or affinity-based sensors for cortisol

subsystems.name: Interstitial fluid access
subsystems.role: brings the fluid being measured into contact with the sensors.
parts: microneedle array (under 1 mm) or microfluidic channels

subsystems.name: Electronics and signal chain
subsystems.role: amplifies tiny sensor currents and voltages and sends them wirelessly.

subsystems.name: Power and housing
subsystems.role: keeps the device running for days on a ring or patch form factor.

subsystems.name: Algorithms and calibration
subsystems.role: turns raw signals into reliable glucose, cortisol and sleep metrics.
parts: signal processing to remove motion and temperature artefacts
machine-learning models trained against blood or lab references

buildSteps.title: Choose sensing chemistry
buildSteps.detail: For glucose, pick an enzyme or optical absorption band; for cortisol, select an antibody, aptamer or molecularly imprinted polymer that binds it selectively.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the sensor array
buildSteps.detail: Print or deposit electrodes on a flexible substrate for electrochemical sensing, or make waveguides and photodiodes for optical sensing.

buildSteps.title: Make the fluid interface
buildSteps.detail: Etch or mould microneedles short enough to reach interstitial fluid without hitting nerves, or pattern microchannels that collect sweat.

buildSteps.title: Assemble electronics
buildSteps.detail: Solder the analog front end, microcontroller and radio onto a flexible circuit, then connect the sensors and battery.

buildSteps.title: Develop algorithms
buildSteps.detail: Collect paired readings (device versus blood draws) from many people, then train models to separate overlapping analyte signals.

buildSteps.title: Package the wearable
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate the electronics in a biocompatible ring or patch, test skin adhesion and ensure it survives washing and sweating.

buildSteps.title: Validate and seek approval
buildSteps.detail: Run clinical studies comparing the device with laboratory standards, then apply for medical-device clearance where the output affects treatment.

prerequisites.tech: Continuous glucose monitoring via interstitial fluid
prerequisites.why: commercial patches already use a tiny filament in interstitial fluid, proving the body-fluid route works for one analyte.
near-infrared and Raman signals from glucose are weak and swamped by water, skin and motion; no consumer device has solved this.
lab prototypes measure cortisol in sweat and interstitial fluid, but they drift, need frequent calibration and are not yet wearable for days.
smartwatches and rings already integrate radios, batteries and sensors in small packages.
dissolving microneedles exist for drug delivery, but a robust array that stays sterile and unclogged for weeks is still research.
sensors respond to several substances at once; untangling glucose from cortisol and other interferents in real time is unsolved.

pathway.milestone: separate wearables track heart rate, sleep and—via invasive patches—glucose
pathway.unlocks: continuous data streams and user habits, but not a single multi-analyte device.

pathway.milestone: research prototypes measure cortisol and glucose together in sweat or interstitial fluid over hours
pathway.unlocks: proof that two analytes can be read from one wearable site.

pathway.milestone: clinical-grade patch integrates glucose, cortisol and sleep algorithms with minimal calibration
pathway.unlocks: monitoring for diabetes, stress and sleep disorders without blood draws.

pathway.milestone: fully non-invasive ring with multi-analyte sensing and closed-loop feedback
pathway.unlocks: personalised dosing or lifestyle advice in real time, if accuracy and biocompatibility hold up.
